normalized.prelim_summary: This one-owner 1987 BMW 325is coupe has stayed in California since new, showing 112k original miles with a clean Carfax and thorough seller documentation. Minor cosmetic flaws and an overdue timing belt are worth budgeting for, but overall it presents as a well-cared-for, desirable manual E30 coupe with factory sport equipment.

critical_evidence.evidence: The listing states the belt was last replaced in 2013, about 13 years ago and far past the 4-5 year interval for the interference M20. The seller says his mechanic told him replacement was not needed. Even if the 2013 invoice exists, the service is overdue, and there is no statement that the water pump or tensioner were done.

The attached underside photo shows only the rear tank, muffler and diff area: dusty, with surface corrosion on the exhaust. Shock towers, rear subframe/trailing-arm mounts, floors, jack points and the trunk battery corner are not examined here. Lifelong California registration lowers but does not remove the risk.
The listing reports no accidents or damage on Carfax, so there is no reported repair to document. Disclosed paint touch-ups and air-dam scrapes should still be checked with a paint meter at the PPI.
There are no records of radiator, expansion tank, thermostat or hose replacement, and no head casting number or overheating history. A 1987 M20B25 may carry a crack-prone early head.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: published VIN matching the decode, original owner, clean CA title in the seller's name, and a Carfax summary with 26 detailed records. The maintenance half is thin: service records are offered but not shown. The only dated item is a 2013 timing belt, and there are no photos of the specific at-risk areas.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight panels, a well-kept Pearl Beige interior with an intact headliner, and a stock engine bay. Observed items are air-dam scrapes, paint touch-ups, a worn wheel and carpet, and past gross-polluter results. The 13-year-old belt and unknown cooling system mean the mechanical condition is unproven.

price_value.rationale: The current $16,000 bid is not the price. The expected hammer sits around the $21,818-$29,887 fair-value band given comparable 325is sales ($26,000-$27,750). The overdue timing belt/water pump is known work that pulls value down.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual, rear-drive, analog car with an easy resale market and a California location fits the brief. However, a 39-year-old car with an overdue belt and an unknown cooling history is not a turnkey reliable bridge. The likely hammer sits above the $10,000-$19,000 ideal band.

logistics.rationale: San Jose is a short drive from Carmel. A PPI at a local BMW independent before the Sept 30 close is realistic if the seller agrees. The car is CA-registered and has passed recent smog.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: It is a 325is with a 5-speed and LSD, Delphin Gray over Pearl Beige sport seats, and the M-Technic I wheel. It is one-owner, essentially stock apart from the stereo, and has the 1984 Olympics plates: several desirable traits together.

what_would_change_verdict: Up: records showing a recent cooling-system refresh and no overheating history, plus a clean combustion-gas test at PPI
Up: lift photos or a PPI showing solid shock towers, subframe mounts and trunk floor
Down: a PPI finding combustion gases in the coolant, a cracked head, or structural rust at the towers or subframe mounts
Down: a seller refusal of pre-close inspection, or an unexplained emissions fault recurring at the PPI sniff test
evidence.mission_note: A manual, rear-drive, stock 325is 75 miles from Carmel fits the point-of-view and resale parts of the brief. As a bridge, its reliability depends on immediately doing the overdue belt/water pump and a cooling and fuel-line catch-up, and the likely hammer sits above the $10,000-$19,000 ideal band.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: a published VIN matching the 1987 325iS decode, one owner since new, lifelong California registration, a clean CA title in the seller's name, and a clean Carfax with 26 detailed records. Photos confirm a stock, desirable spec — Delphin Gray over Pearl Beige sport seats, 5-speed, basketweave wheels — with an aftermarket stereo the only visible change. The listing itself establishes known work: the timing belt was last replaced in 2013, roughly 13 years ago on an interference engine, and the seller declined replacement on his mechanic's advice. It also discloses air-dam scrapes and paint touch-ups, and 2015/2017 gross-polluter designations whose cause is not explained. The service records are offered but not shown, so cooling-system history, head casting, fuel lines and bushings remain open. The underside evidence is limited to a single rear view with no visible rot. The $16,000 current bid is well below the $21,818-$29,887 fair-value band, but comparable 325is sales suggest the hammer will land near that band.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller through BaT today requesting the 2013 belt invoice, cooling-system records, the gross-polluter repair invoice and underbody photos, and ask to book a PPI at a San Jose BMW independent before the Sept 30, 14:01 close.
